howto:tag_checklist.body:
h4. Tagging Checklist

[expand=Table of Contents]
* [0. Basic Identification](#dtext-lv0)
** [0-i. Explicit](#dtext-lv0-1)
** [0-ii. Information and Requests](#dtext-lv0-2)
** [0-iii. Technical Information and Source](#dtext-lv0-3)
* [1. Composition and Foreground Details](#dtext-lv1)
* [2. Background Details and Artistic Errors](#dtext-lv2)
* [3. Additional Details, Canons, Memes](#dtext-lv3)
* [4. Microscopic Details](#dtext-lv4)
[/expand]

This tag checklist exists as a reference for commonly used tags for new and existing uploaders alike. The list is organized into levels, with lower levels representing the essential tags, and higher levels representing niche tags that may be more difficult to apply correctly.

Please feel free to take your time getting used to memorizing this list. As a general rule, all uploads are expected to be tagged to at least Level 1 of the checklist.

[quote]
[b]Note to taggers:[/b] Some parts of this checklist may be incomplete. Feel free to help out with expanding the checklist, however, if any part of this list grows too large, please inform the forums about creating a tag group. Remember to reference this tagging checklist!
[/quote]

h4. Things Not to Tag

[b]Subjective tags[/b] that express opinions or subjective critique on images. Common examples are badass, cute, good, evil, moe, sexy and most other adjectives. A full list of known subjective tags may be found at [[Tag group:Subjective]].

Avoid making tags for themes that can be easily represented as individual tags:

* Blondes in bikinis {{blonde_hair bikini}}
* Bloody fighting: {{battle blood}}
* Sleepy in the morning: {{sleepy morning}}

Note that these searches are possible from a basic Member account, with a two-tag search limit, even if a little browsing may be required.

h4#lv0. Level 0: Basic Identification

Level 0 is the baseline of acceptable tagging - all posts must be tagged to at least this level. Adding these tags enables basic searchability.

h6. Identification

* [b]Artist[/b] (prefix with artist: when creating a new tag)
** If the artist does not currently have a tag on Danbooru, consider creating a new one. If you don't know how to read their name to create a tag, consider asking in the forum topic "Artist tagging help":/forum_topics/8199, where someone is likely to help you come up with a name for the tag.
* [b]Copyright[/b] (prefix with copyright: when creating a new tag)
* [b]Character[/b] (prefix with character: when creating a new tag) 
** Character lists from popular copyrights are available at [[tag groups]], in the Characters section.
* [b]Source[/b]
* [[original]]
** Use this tag for illustrations that feature characters that are not related to any kind of copyright.
** Frequently, these characters appear only in the one illustration, and will not have a name. In these cases, it isn't necessary to include character tags for them; the [[original]] tag is enough.
** Sometimes, such a character may become recurring, limited to a single artist, or multiple artists on a very small scale. (In this case, they may have names. Most such named original characters can be found listed on the wiki page of the artist that created them.)

h6. Classification

* [b]Rating[/b]
** See: [[howto:rate]]
** (use the [b]Ratings[/b] choice list, or use {{rating:e}}, {{rating:q}}, {{rating:s}} or {{rating:g}}).
* [[Spoilers]] (Important: apply if image is a potential spoiler)
[spoiler]Let's keep Danbooru a spoiler-free community.[/spoiler]

h6. Basic Image Content

* [b]Character Counters[/b]
** [[1boy]] | [[2boys|2]], [[3boys|3]], [[4boys|4]], [[5boys|5]], [[6+boys]]
** [[1girl]] | [[2girls|2]], [[3girls|3]], [[4girls|4]], [[5girls|5]], [[6+girls]]
** [[1other]] | [[2others|2]], [[3others|3]], [[4others|4]], [[5others|5]], [[6+others]]
** [[solo]] - single character, mutually exclusive with multiple copies of a character e.g. [[multiple views]] 
*** [[solo focus]] - multiple characters, focus on a single character
* [b]Framing[/b]
** [[close-up]]
** [[portrait]] - shoulders or above
*** [[head out of frame]] - shoulders or below
** [[upper body]] - above waist
*** [[lower body]] - below waist
** [[cowboy shot]] - above knees
** [[feet out of frame]] - above ankles
** [[full body]] - full body visible, close range
** [[wide shot]] - full body visible, far range
* [b]Viewpoint[/b]
** [[straight-on]]
** [[from above]]
** [[from behind]]
** [[from below]]
** [[from side]]
** [[pov]]
* [b]Actions/Posture[/b], see [[tag group:posture]]
** [[battle]]
** [[chasing]]
** [[fighting]]
** [[kneeling]]
** [[leaning]]
** [[lying]]
** [[running]]
** [[sitting]]
** [[squatting]]
** [[standing]]
** [[walking]]
* [b]Face[/b], see [[tag group:face tags]]
** Eyes, see [[tag group:eyes tags]]
* [b]Facial Expressions[/b], see [[tag group:face tags]]
** See [[tag group:eyes tags]], in the Emotions section.
** See [[tag group:face tags]], in the Emotes section.
* [b]Body Colors[/b]

** Skin Color, see [[tag group:skin color]]

h4#lv0-1. Level 0-i: Explicit

These are basic tags specific to explicit or graphic images.
[b]Important Note:[/b] If any of these tags are applied to an image, [b]consider setting the Rating to Questionable or Explicit[/b], as it will often (but not always) be appropriate, and Danbooru does not automatically do it for you. See [[howto:rate]] for precise guidelines regarding ratings.

* [b]Age[/b]
** [[loli]]

* [b]Cum/Ejaculation[/b]
** [[cum]]
* [b]Body Parts,[/b] see [[tag group:body parts]]

* [b]Sexual Actions,[/b] see [[tag group:sex acts]]

* [b]Sexual Positions,[/b] see [[tag group:sexual positions]]

* [b]Sexual Themes,[/b] see [[tag group:sex acts]]
** [[bdsm]]

* [b]Sexual Objects,[/b] see [[tag group:sex objects]]

* [b]Relationships[/b] (if applicable)
** [[futa with futa]] 
** [[futa with female]]

* [b]Graphic Content[/b]
** [[guro]] (Important: commonly blacklisted tag)

h4#lv0-2. Level 0-ii: Information and Requests

These tags indicate if additional information about an image, such as translations or artist commentaries are available.

h6. Information Present

* [[translated]]
** To be added only when the image is considered fully translated, see [[howto:translate|Translation Guidelines]].
* [[commentary]]
** To be added if a commentary fully understandable by an English speaker is present, or when it has been fully translated into English.

h6. Requests

* [[artist request]]
** To be added and retained until the artist has been identified.
* [[character request]]
** To be added and retained until all characters, foreground or background have been identified.
* [[commentary request]]
* [[translation request]]
** [[partially translated]]
** These tags to be added and retained until image is considered fully translated, see [[howto:translate|Translation Guidelines]].


h4#lv0-3. Level 0-iii: Technical Image Information and Source

These tags are to used to identify specifications of an image such as pixel size (dimensions), file sizes and types of sources.

* [b]Image Sizes[/b] 
** [i]Image size tags are now applied automatically.[/i]
* [b]Illustration Source[/b]
** [[comic]]
** [[commissioner upload]]
** [[scan]]
** [[self-upload]] 


h4#lv1. Level 1: Composition and Foreground Graphic Details

These tags are used to identify things happening in the foreground. Adding these tags brings Danbooru to an acceptable level of searchability.

* [b]Against[/b]

** [[against tree]]
* [b]Composition and Artistic Genre[/b]
** [[landscape]]
** [[no humans]]

* [b]Character Archetypes, Jobs and Classes[/b] see [[tag group:jobs]]

* [b]Gestures,[/b] see [[tag group:gestures]]
* [b]Generic Character Groupings and Pairings[/b]
** [[couple]]

**** Special tag, due to the majority of Danbooru posts featuring female characters. The [[female focus]] tag is to be left unused.
** [[harem]]

* [b]Objects in Foreground or Held or Operated by Characters[/b]
** Audio Equipment, see [[tag group:audio tags]]
** Musical Equipment, see [[tag group:audio tags]]
* [b]Legendary Creatures,[/b] see [[tag group:legendary creatures]]
** Includes supernatural humanoids or 'races' such as [[demon]], [[angel]], [[dragon]]...
* [b]Wear/Costume (Accessories)[/b]
** [[hair ornament]]


h4#lv2. Level 2: Background Graphic Details and Artistic Errors

These tags identify things happening in the background. Adding these tags greatly enhance Danbooru's searchability, possibly to the level of professional image databases such as GettyImages.

* [b]Age[/b]

** Note: Error tags are the only technically subjective tags approved for use on Danbooru, due to their relations with the highly subjective nature of the [[help:mod queue|Moderation Queue]].

* [b]Time of Day[/b]

* [b]Weather[/b]

h4#lv3. Level 3: Additional Artistic Details, Canons and Memes

These tags are for those with an intimate knowledge of the images they are searching for, such as artistic techniques, celebrities and family relationships.

* [b]Celebrities/Real World People,[/b] see [[tag group:people]]
* [b]Characters, Implied[/b]
** [[animalization]]
** [[objectification]]
** [[personification]]
** Example: Cake Representing Patchouli Knowledge, Post #495479
** Example: Cockroach Representing Wriggle Nightbug (meme), Post #594819
* [b]Family Relationships,[/b] see [[tag group:family relationships]]
** Note: requires intimate knowledge of 
* [b]Medium, Traditional[/b]
** [[traditional media]]
** [[marker (medium)]]
** [[watercolor (medium)]]
** [[graphite (medium)]]
** These tags are only for art created without a computer (bar scanning or photography). They usually carry a suffix (medium) to resolve ambiguities with many tags.
* [b]Artistic Technique, Method of Creation/Preparation[/b]
** [[3D]]
** [[oekaki]]
** [[pixel art]]
* [b]Text and Languages[/b]
** [[chinese text]]
** [[korean text]]
*** hangul (use [[korean_text]])
** [[english text]]
** [[russian text]]
* [b]Timestamps[/b]
** see [[Tag group:Year tags]]

h4#lv4. Level 4: Microscopic Details

These tags identify extremely minute details in the background, often missed by a glance. The importance of tagging these details may be under debate, as they can either make or break the searchability of our images depending on the situation.

* Characters that appear far in the background
* Characters which are only partially visible
* Characters whose point of view is the subject of the image

h4. See Also

* [[howto:tag|Tagging Guidelines]]
* [[Tag groups|Tag Groups]]

list of commonly misused tags.body:
h4. Mutually exclusive tags

The following cannot be used to describe the same object or situation

* [[ambiguous gender]] <-> [[androgynous]]
* [[bare pectorals]] <-> ([[topless male]], [[nude]], [[breastless clothes]] or [[underwear only]])
* [[bottomless]] <-> [[bare legs]] 
* [[greyscale]] <-> [[grey theme]]
* [[hands in opposite sleeves]] <-> [[sleeves past wrists]]
* [[hairband]] <-> [[headband]]
* [[jersey]] <-> [[track jacket]]
* [[looking at viewer]] <-> ([[facing viewer]] or [[closed eyes]] or [[blindfold]])
* [[nude]] <-> ([[bare shoulders]] or [[bare legs]] or [[bare arms]] or [[topless female]] or [[bottomless]])
* [[official alternate costume]] <-> [[alternate costume]]
** [[official alternate hairstyle]] <-> [[alternate hairstyle]]
* ([[off-shoulder shirt]]/[[off-shoulder dress|dress]]/[[off-shoulder sweater|sweater]]) <-> ([[strapless]] [[strapless shirt|shirt]]/[[strapless dress|dress]] or [[tube top]]) <-> ([[sleeveless]] [[sleeveless shirt|shirt]]/[[sleeveless dress|dress]]/[[sleeveless sweater|sweater]])
* [[playboy bunny]] <-> ([[kittysuit]] or [[rabbit costume]])
* [[solo]] <-> ([[solo focus]] or [[multiple views]])
* [[topless female]] <-> ([[nude]] or [[bare shoulders]] or [[bare arms]])
* [[x-ray]] <-> [[cross-section]]
* [[miko]] <-> [[nontraditional miko]]

h4. Specific mistagging

h5. Places

* [[changing room]]/[[dressing room]]/[[fitting room]]/[[locker room]]
** Not to be used interchangeably for just any rooms where a character would get dressed and/or undressed.
** [[Changing room]]s are the ones where people remove and store their clothes, usually when going to a [[pool]] or an [[onsen]].
** [[Dressing room]]s are the ones used by on-stage performers to change in and out of their costumes.
** [[Fitting room]]s are the tiny ones in clothing stores where individual customers can try on clothes before buying them.
** [[Locker room]]s are similar to changing rooms, but [[locker]]s must be visible.

h5. Objects

* [[animal ears]]
** Do not use for actual animals, which have these by default.
* [[costume switch]]
** Applicable only if there are multiple characters, to be sure there is a switch.
** Not applicable on single-character [[cosplay]] pictures. Add the appropriate cosplay tag instead.
** Not applicable on parent-child pairs of single-character [[cosplay]] posts.
** Not the same as a "costume change."
* [[crescent moon]]
** Do not tag for just [[crescent]] shaped objects, e.g. [[crescent hair ornament]]
* [[goat horns]]
** Commonly mistagged on [[sheep horns]]. Goat horns traditionally do not curl all the way around.
* [[naked towel]]
** Character must be wearing the towel, not just having it on their person
* [[off-shoulder jacket]]/[[off-shoulder coat]]/[[off-shoulder cardigan]]
** Should be used when the jacket, coat, or cardigan is naturally designed with a low and wide-cut neckline.
** Do not use for open/partially open jackets/coats/cardigans that are simply worn hanging off the upper arms.
* [[red glasses]]
** See either [[red-framed eyewear]] or [[red-tinted eyewear]]
* [[see-through clothes]]/[[transparent]]
** See-through is for clothing, transparent is for other objects.
* [[short hair]]
** Not for [[medium hair|shoulder-length hair]]
* [[silhouette]]
** Not for mere [[shadow]]s behind objects; should be mostly featureless
* [[vaginal]]
** If female character's genital is visible, tagging [[pussy]] is mandatory. 
* [[miko]]
** Only to be used if a character is wearing the actual traditional outfit of a miko: a [[hakama skirt]] (almost always entirely red) and white kosode or kimono. Otherwise, use [[nontraditional miko]] instead.

h5. Actions

* [[squirting liquid]]
** Not for [[female ejaculation]]
* [[facing viewer]]
** Only for characters with [[closed eyes|closed]] or [[covered eyes]]
* [[floating]]
** When on water, use [[afloat]] instead
* [[partially submerged]]
** Not for just [[sitting]] in [[shallow water]]
* [[air guitar]]
** This is for pretending to play a guitar [i]without holding anything[/i]. Pretending to play guitar with anything but a guitar is using an [[unconventional guitar]].
* [[riding]]
** Only for characters riding an [[animal]] or a [[motor vehicle]], use [[girl on top]] or [[boy on top]], and [[cowgirl position]] for posts depicting a person having sex on top of another person.
* [[takeoff]]
** Only for characters or [[aircraft]]s leaving the ground. Use [[undressing]] for images depicting someone taking off their clothes.

h5. Miscellaneous

* [[casual]]
** Not for characters that always appear in casual clothing
* [[contemporary]]
** Not for characters that always appear in contemporary settings
* [[couple]]
** Applies whenever characters are intended by the artist to be a romantic couple and are shown in a romantic light; should not be used on images of characters having sex with no implications of romance
* [[furrification]]
** Applies to human or non-furry humanoid characters being turned into furries. Non-anthropohmorphic [[Pokemon]] and other creatures being drawn as furries is [[personification]].
* [[gothic punk]]
** A specific style of j-fashion, does not mean "[[goth fashion|goth]] + [[punk]]"
* [[humanization]]
** Refers to characters that were already humanoid to begin with being depicted as fully human; depictions of non-humanoids as humans belong under [[personification]]
* [[no humans]]
** Does not apply to human-like characters such as [[humanoid robot]]s and [[furry|furries]].
* [[orc]] and [[ogre]]
** Orcs are commonly depicted with a green-skinned muscular or chubby body and sports a tusks, while ogres usually have a fat body and lacks any tusks.
* [[text focus]]
** Only when text is a major component of an image

h4. See also

* topic #14603 (Commonly misused tags)
* [[help:tasks]]
